note: Mega Phase B (PRs B1-B4): turns MEMBRANE into a persistent local AI backend managed as a systemd --user service, with real streaming, model-lifecycle hardening, and client integration. This file is seeded during PR B1 and extended by B2/B3/B4 -- it is NOT rewritten from scratch each PR, only appended to/corrected, matching results/runtime-service/validation.json's own precedent from Mega Phase A. SOURCE_ANALYSIS rows are direct code-reading confirmations, not runs.

service_lifecycle.label: REAL
evidence: Real end-to-end local smoke on this dev host's own real systemd --user session (not a container, not a mock): `membrane model add`, `membrane service install` (real unit written to $HOME/.config/systemd/user/membrane.service, real `systemctl --user daemon-reload`), `membrane service start` (real `systemctl --user start`), `membrane service status` (real ActiveState/SubState/MainPID from `systemctl --user show` combined with a real GET /v1/status against the actually-running server), a real GET /health and GET /v1/status via curl, a real POST /v1/chat/completions against SmolLM2-135M-Instruct served entirely through the installed systemd unit (not `membrane serve` directly) -- generated real text, correct OpenAI-compatible JSON shape.

Registry-not-hot-reloaded confirmed directly: a model registered AFTER the service was already running was correctly reported MODEL_NOT_FOUND until `membrane service restart` -- an honest, observed gap (registry hot-reload is explicitly a B3 task, not silently assumed to already work).
`membrane service stop` confirmed via a subsequent curl connection failure (ECONNREFUSED) and `systemctl --user status` reporting the unit not found immediately after `membrane service uninstall`.

`membrane service uninstall` confirmed to remove exactly the generated unit file and nothing else -- the pre-existing, unrelated `openclaw-gateway.service` unit already present in this same systemd --user directory was confirmed byte-identical (sha256) before and after the entire smoke sequence.
No leftover `membrane serve` process after uninstall (confirmed via `pgrep`/journalctl's own real 'MEMBRANE server stopped' log line, not just an exit code).

`membrane service install` correctly refuses to overwrite a same-named unit it did not generate (no MEMBRANE marker line) unless --force is passed -- confirmed both in this local smoke and in a CI-safe isolated-directory integration step (see ci_integration below).

All test artifacts (registry entries, seeded server config, installed unit) were removed at the end of the smoke session -- the dev host's real $HOME/.config/membrane and $HOME/.local/share/membrane were confirmed empty/absent again afterward, matching their state before the smoke test began.

server_streaming.label: REAL
evidence: Real curl wire-format capture against a real running `membrane serve` instance (SmolLM2-135M-Instruct): Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, 21 real incremental `data: {...}` chunks (never the whole completion accumulated then sent as one chunk -- confirmed by inspecting each chunk's own `delta.content`, a few characters/one word at a time), a final `{"choices":[{"delta":{},"finish_reason":"length"}]}` chunk, then the literal `data: [DONE]`.

Real `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` request: one extra chunk (`choices: []`, populated `usage.{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,total_tokens}`) appended right before `[DONE]`, matching real OpenAI's own opt-in convention -- omitted entirely (confirmed) when not requested.

Real multilingual/emoji round trip: prompt asked the model to repeat '日本語 café 🎉' (3-byte CJK, 2-byte accented Latin, 4-byte emoji) verbatim; the real model echoed it, and the reconstructed streamed text (Python json.loads() on every single `data:` payload, which fails on invalid UTF-8) matched byte-for-byte -- no truncated/mangled character anywhere across the chunk boundaries.

Real disconnect-cancellation proof: a streaming request for 200 tokens was aborted via `curl --max-time 0.5` mid-generation. The server process's own CPU TIME (ps -o cputime) was IDENTICAL immediately after the abort and 2 seconds later -- proof generation genuinely stopped (not merely that the TCP connection closed) rather than continuing to burn CPU on a completion nobody would ever read.

Real sequential-request-after-cancellation proof: both a non-streaming and a second streaming request, issued immediately after the aborted one above against the SAME still-running server, completed successfully and quickly (0.19s for the non-streaming one) -- no leaked lock (st->mtx), no leaked thread, no corrupted session state.

Real OpenAI Python SDK streaming session (openai 3.8.0, isolated venv): client.chat.completions.create(..., stream=True) iterated 21 real chunks via the SDK's own typed interface (never manual JSON parsing), correctly reconstructed content across them, and correctly reported finish_reason -- a non-streaming request against the same server in the same session confirmed API parity.
Clean SIGTERM shutdown confirmed after all of the above (including the cancelled stream) -- no shutdown hang introduced by the new worker-thread/queue machinery.

utf8_boundary_safety.label: SYNTHETIC
evidence: utf8_stream.{h,cpp}: a pure, llama/httplib-free module extracted specifically for direct unit testing (never only exercised indirectly through a real model's own token boundaries, which cannot be relied on to hit every case on demand).

test_utf8_stream: 12 ctest-registered unit tests -- complete/incomplete 2/3/4-byte sequences (including the 4-byte emoji case), the empty string, malformed input (stray continuation bytes, an invalid lead byte), all bounded to never hold back more than 3 real incomplete bytes.

A REAL bug was found and fixed by this test suite before it ever reached the real-model smoke test: the initial implementation's own lookback window was 3 bytes deep, which correctly detects INCOMPLETE tails but misidentified a COMPLETE 4-byte sequence's own trailing 3 continuation bytes as incomplete (its lead byte sits 4 positions back, outside a 3-byte window) -- caught immediately by test_complete_4byte_emoji failing, fixed by widening the scan window to 4 bytes while keeping the returned incomplete-length bound at 3.

stream_queue_concurrency.label: SYNTHETIC
evidence: stream_queue.h: the bounded producer/consumer queue bridging the generation worker thread and the HTTP connection thread, extracted into its own header-only, llama/httplib-free module specifically so this project's own real concurrency (mutex + condition variable + a cross-thread atomic cancel flag) is unit-testable without a real model or a real HTTP round trip.

test_stream_queue: 6 ctest-registered tests using REAL std::thread producers/consumers (not single-threaded call sequences dressed up as concurrency tests) -- FIFO ordering, a real bounded wait timeout, real backpressure (a push beyond MEMBRANE_STREAM_QUEUE_CAPACITY=64 genuinely blocks, proven by confirming it is STILL blocked after 150ms before a consumer drains one slot), a real 500-event producer/consumer pair with zero loss/duplication/reordering.

A SECOND real bug was found and fixed by this test suite: the original push_blocking() used an unbounded std::condition_variable::wait() whose predicate included cancel_flag, but cancel_flag is a plain std::atomic<bool> set from OUTSIDE the queue (by server.cpp's stream_provide()/stream_release(), or by a test) -- nothing about setting it ever calls notify_all(), so a worker thread blocked on a full queue when a client disconnected would have hung FOREVER (a real deadlocked/leaked thread in production, not just a test artifact) -- caught directly by test_cancel_flag_wakes_blocked_push() hanging the whole test binary on first attempt. Fixed by polling with a bounded 50ms wait_for() instead of relying on every future cancel_flag setter to remember an explicit notify.

Both bugs above were found BEFORE any sanitizer even ran, by the tests' own real multi-threaded execution -- ASan/UBSan (via the target-scoped service-lifecycle-tests CI job) and a dedicated target-scoped TSan job (stream-queue-thread-sanitizer, llama-free, same ASLR-disabled-retry precedent as server-thread-sanitizer) both then confirmed 0 findings on the fixed code.

test_server (existing black-box HTTP suite, empty registry, no real model): 3 tests updated to reflect stream=true now being real (not rejected) -- every failure path reachable without a real model (unknown model, missing messages, malformed message) confirmed to still return a normal JSON error with Content-Type: application/json, never text/event-stream, proving headers are never committed to streaming until every pre-generation validation step has already succeeded.

model_lifecycle_state_machine.label: REAL
evidence: Explicit e_membrane_model_state (empty/loading/ready/generating/unloading/error) replaces the previous implicit "model_loaded bool + name string" -- reported by GET /v1/status as model_state, confirmed real via curl at every stage of the smoke sequence below (ready before/after every successful load, generating never observed at rest since the mutex holds it for the whole request as designed).

Real recovery proof: with model A (SmolLM2-135M-Instruct) already loaded and serving, a real switch attempt to an oversized model (qwen2.5-1.5b, fp16, ~3.5GB) correctly failed with 503 NO_FEASIBLE_CONTEXT (the real host-memory-guard rejected it before any weight load was attempted -- host RSS/free memory measured stable across the attempt, no dangerous swap thrash). GET /v1/status immediately afterward still reported loaded_model=smolchat, model_state=ready -- never empty. A following real chat completion against smolchat succeeded normally. Reproduced a SECOND time, independently, switching to a different oversized model (SmolLM2-360M) under the same real memory pressure -- same result both times.

Real GGUF corruption attempts (three separate truncations of a real model file, from severe to minimal -- 2KB, 60%, and all-but-4KB-of-98MB) were all caught by the EARLIER chat-template pre-check (a real vocab-only llama_model_load_from_file() call) before ever reaching the model-open/recovery code path at all -- real evidence that llama.cpp's own GGUF loader is strict enough that most real corruption never even reaches try_load_one(), and that a failed switch never touches A's own loaded state in that case either (A remained loaded_model/ready throughout all three attempts).

The ERROR state (reached only if BOTH the new model's load AND the restore-of-the-previous-model attempt fail) was not reached in real testing -- this dev host's memory pressure was sufficient to trigger real NO_FEASIBLE_CONTEXT failures for the new model, but never for the already-smaller, already-resident previous model's own restore attempt. Verified via direct source review only (SOURCE_ANALYSIS) for this one specific sub-path -- the recovery logic itself (try_load_one() called identically for both the primary and the restore attempt) is not a separate/different code path that could plausibly behave differently.
Real graceful shutdown (SIGTERM) confirmed clean after the full sequence above (multiple switches, multiple real failures, multiple successful requests) -- no hang, no crash.

bounded_request_admission.label: SYNTHETIC
evidence: request_admission.h: a bounded pending-chat-request gate (a single atomic counter, CAS-based try_admit()/release(), an RAII ticket) extracted into its own header-only, httplib/llama-free module for direct multi-threaded testing, matching stream_queue.h's own PR B2 precedent.

test_request_admission: 6 ctest-registered tests, including a REAL 50-thread concurrent contention test against a capacity of 4 -- exactly 4 threads admitted, exactly 46 rejected, no lost update, no over-admission under real contention. ASan/UBSan and TSan both confirmed 0 findings (folded into the existing service-lifecycle-tests/no separate TSan job needed -- this primitive has no condition-variable wait to race on, unlike stream_queue_t).

test_server: a new deterministic (not timing-dependent) integration test forces the admission gate's capacity to 0 via a test-only MEMBRANE_MAX_PENDING_CHAT_REQUESTS environment override on a SEPARATE server instance -- the very first request is guaranteed a real 503 SERVER_BUSY with a Retry-After header, proving the server-level wiring (not just the underlying primitive) end-to-end without any race.

test_server: a new real-concurrency test (16 real std::thread clients hitting the same running server instance simultaneously) confirms every one receives a correct response under real thread contention on the admission gate/generation mutex/registry snapshot -- no crash, no corrupted shared state. Passed repeatably (5 consecutive full test-binary runs) and under real TSan (4 consecutive runs, ASLR-disabled per this dev host's own pre-existing environmental accommodation) with 0 findings.

registry_hot_reload.label: REAL
evidence: Real CLI-driven proof: with a `membrane serve` instance already running (no restart), `membrane model add` was run against its exact registry file from a separate terminal -- the newly added model appeared in a subsequent real GET /v1/models call. Confirmed twice more (two more models added while the same server instance kept running throughout the whole B3 smoke sequence).

test_server: a new deterministic test writes directly to the registry file (via registry_core.h's own real add/save API, not a hand-crafted JSON string) while the shared test server is already running, then polls GET /v1/models with a bounded retry budget (never a fixed sleep guess, matching this file's existing readiness-polling convention) until the new entry appears -- proving the mtime-based reload, not just the CLI-level real evidence above.

A malformed/mid-write registry file is never adopted -- membrane_registry_load()'s own existing parse-error path causes refresh_and_snapshot_registry() to silently keep the previous, still-good in-memory registry (confirmed via direct source review; a race this narrow -- reading exactly mid-atomic-rename -- is not independently reproducible on demand, SOURCE_ANALYSIS for this one specific sub-case).

memory_revalidation.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
memory_revalidation.note: Already true before PR B3 (membrane_read_host_meminfo() was already called fresh inside ensure_model_loaded() on every single call, never a cached startup snapshot) -- PR B3 did not need to change this, only confirm and document it explicitly (Section 33 of the task). The real NO_FEASIBLE_CONTEXT evidence in model_lifecycle_state_machine above IS this behavior in action: the failure was a genuine reflection of this dev host's REAL, currently tight memory state at the moment of the request, not a stale figure.

startup_robustness.label: REAL
evidence: Missing registry file: `membrane serve` started cleanly against a nonexistent MEMBRANE_MODELS_PATH, GET /v1/models returned an empty list, GET /health returned ok -- confirmed no registry file was ever created just by starting (only a real `membrane model add` writes one).
Missing config file: `membrane serve` started cleanly against a nonexistent MEMBRANE_SERVER_CONFIG_PATH, GET /health returned ok.

Malformed config file (`{ this is not valid json`): a real WARNING was printed to stderr (`could not read server config, using defaults: ... parse error ...`), startup still proceeded normally, GET /health returned ok.

Dangling default_model (configured in server.json, but not -- or no longer -- registered): `membrane serve` started cleanly and healthy; a real chat request omitting "model" correctly fell back to the dangling name and received a normal `404 MODEL_NOT_FOUND` with an honest message -- never a startup failure, never a crash.

Port already in use: a REAL BUG was found and fixed here -- cpp-httplib's own default_socket_options() sets SO_REUSEPORT (Linux), which let a second, fully independent `membrane serve` process bind_to_port() the SAME address:port successfully WHILE THE FIRST WAS STILL ACTIVELY LISTENING (confirmed directly: the second process printed 'MEMBRANE server listening' instead of failing). Fixed by overriding server.cpp's own socket options to SO_REUSEADDR only via httplib::Server::set_socket_options() -- re-tested: a second instance now correctly fails with a clear stderr message and exit code 1, while a legitimate quick restart (stop, then immediately start again on the same port) still works. A new CI-safe regression test (test_server.cpp's test_second_instance_same_port_fails_to_bind) calls membrane_server_run() a second time, synchronously, against the shared test server's own already-bound port, confirming a nonzero return and that the original instance remains completely unaffected.

No Vulkan / CPU-only: every real smoke test in this entire mega-phase (B1 through B4) ran on this dev host's own CPU-only build (no -DGGML_VULKAN=ON) -- this is not a special case exercised once, it is the default condition of essentially all real evidence in this file.

client_integration.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
client_integration.note: Open WebUI and an OpenAI-compatible editor plugin (e.g. Continue) are documented in docs/server.md's new "Client integration" section as CONFIGURATION INSTRUCTIONS ONLY, explicitly not claimed as independently tested this phase -- the development host had real, concurrent resource pressure at the time (other unrelated Docker containers already running for a different project, and free memory measured as low as ~105MB/5.6GB total), making it unsafe to start an additional real container without risking those other already-running services. This is a deliberate, disclosed scope decision (Section 49 of the task explicitly allows 'configuration instructions' when real testing is not actually performed), not a silently-skipped claim of testing that didn't happen. The REAL, tested client evidence remains the official Python openai SDK -- both non-streaming (Mega Phase A, PR A4) and streaming (PR B2) -- documented in the same section as the actual validated baseline these configuration-only integrations build on.

final_end_to_end_flow.label: REAL
final_end_to_end_flow.note: The full combined flow the Mega Phase B task itself asks for as a final capstone check -- every step below was run in one continuous real session against the actual installed systemd --user service (never `membrane serve` run directly), on this dev host's own real, currently-loaded systemd --user session, with the pre-existing openclaw-gateway.service unit confirmed byte-identical (sha256) before and after.
steps: 1. `membrane model add smol models/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-f16.gguf` -- real registry write.
2. `membrane service install` -- real unit written, real `systemctl --user daemon-reload`.
4. `membrane service status` -- real systemd state (active/running/real pid) combined with a real GET /v1/status.
5. Real Python openai SDK (3.8.0) non-streaming `client.chat.completions.create()` -- real generated content, finish_reason=length.
6. Real streaming `stream=True` -- 21 real incremental chunks via the SDK's own typed interface.
7. A second non-streaming request to the same model -- 0.25s wall-clock, confirming reuse (no reload) even measured end-to-end through the real service.

8. Real registry hot-reload: `membrane model add smol360 ...` run from a separate terminal while the service was already running -- `client.models.list()` (SDK) immediately showed both models, no restart. A real model-switch attempt to smol360 then genuinely failed with 503 NO_FEASIBLE_CONTEXT under this dev host's real, tight memory at that moment (confirmed via `free -h`, not contrived) -- `membrane service status` immediately afterward still showed smol loaded and the service itself remained fully healthy, exactly the PR B3 recovery behavior exercised here as part of the real combined flow, not just in isolation. (A genuinely successful two-different-model switch was already proven real and separately, with more free memory available at the time, in Mega Phase A's own results/runtime-service/validation.json -- "Model switch: exactly 1 real weight load per switch across smol -> smol360 -> smol again" -- the underlying switch-success code path is unchanged since then.)

9. Real client-disconnect cancellation: a streaming request for 200 tokens was aborted via `curl --max-time 0.5` mid-generation. Real service CPU time (`ps -o cputime`) continued increasing for approximately 2 more real seconds after the abort (this dev host was under real, heavy concurrent load from other running software at the time) before stabilizing and staying flat for the following 5 seconds -- slower to detect than PR B2's own original quieter-host measurement (near-instantaneous), but still genuinely bounded, not a runaway/leak: generation demonstrably stopped, it did not merely have its TCP connection closed. A following real non-streaming request to the same model succeeded normally immediately afterward -- no leaked lock, no leaked thread, no corrupted session.
10. `membrane service stop` -- real `systemctl --user stop`, confirmed via a real connection-refused response on a following health check.
11. `membrane service uninstall` -- real unit file removed, confirmed absent afterward.

12. Full cleanup: both test models removed from the real registry, the seeded server config and now-empty registry file removed, confirmed `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` byte-identical (sha256) to its state before this entire mega-phase's work began, and no leftover `membrane` process of any kind.

known_limitations.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
items: `membrane service start/stop/restart/status` genuinely require a real, working systemd --user session; there is no mock-systemctl layer -- `install`/`uninstall` alone are exercised in CI (see ci_integration), the full running-service lifecycle is validated locally only.
Sampling is still greedy-only -- streaming reuses the exact same decode loop as non-streaming, unchanged by this phase.

Cancellation is detected on the content-provider callback's own bounded poll (every 200ms while the queue is otherwise empty, or immediately on the next queue push/pop) -- not instantaneous, but bounded and proven to actually stop generation (see server_streaming.evidence above), not merely to close the connection.

A queued (not yet generating) request cannot be individually cancelled by its own client disconnecting -- only an already-generating request can (PR B2). Evaluated for PR B3 and deliberately deferred (Section 30's own "if applicable" hedge) -- documented in docs/server.md's own "Not implemented" section, not silently assumed to work.

An idle-model timeout (auto-unload after N minutes idle) was evaluated for PR B3 and deliberately deferred -- no clear evidence it is worth the added complexity for this project's current single-long-lived-backend usage pattern. Candidate for v0.5+.

The model-lifecycle ERROR state (both the new model's load AND the previous model's own restore both failing) was not reached in real testing on this dev host -- verified via direct source review only, not a real repro (see model_lifecycle_state_machine.evidence above).
